An isolated VirtualBox lab with Kali Linux for ethical hacking and penetration-testing practice

SkillCybersecurityVirtualBox7.2Kali Linux2026.1Network10.0.0.0/24NetworkwalksWeek 1

About

This is my Week 1 project for the Networkwalks Cybersecurity programme (task WK1-PM1). I built a self-contained testing lab on my own laptop: VirtualBox as the hypervisor, Kali Linux as the attacking machine, and a private NAT Network that every future lab machine can join.

Everything here is documented step by step with the screenshots I took while building it, including the mistakes I hit and how I fixed them.

Ethical use only. Everything in this lab is confined to machines I own inside the lab. None of it may be used against systems without explicit written permission.

Lab design

                    Windows 11 host (Dell Latitude 7390, 8 GB RAM)
        +--------------------------------------------------------------+
        |                    Oracle VirtualBox 7.2                     |
        |                                                              |
        |   NatNetwork  10.0.0.0/24   (DHCP enabled, gateway 10.0.0.1)  |
        |   ----------------------------------------------------------  |
        |        |                                                     |
        |   +----------------------+                                   |
        |   | Kali Linux 2026.1    |      (future VMs: Windows 7/10/11, |
        |   | 10.0.0.2/24          |       Android, Server 2016 ...)    |
        |   +----------------------+                                   |
        +-------------------|------------------------------------------+
                            |
                     NAT to the internet

Why a NAT Network rather than plain NAT: machines on the same NAT Network can talk to each other and still reach the internet, which is exactly what a multi-VM practice lab needs. Plain NAT gives every VM its own isolated network.

Setup walkthrough

Step 1. Install 7-Zip

Kali is distributed as a compressed archive, so 7-Zip is needed to extract the VM image. Download: https://7-zip.org/download.html. I used the 64-bit Windows x64 installer.

Step 2. Install VirtualBox

VirtualBox is the hypervisor that runs the lab. Download: https://virtualbox.org/wiki/Downloads. Choose the Windows hosts installer and accept the defaults.

Step 3. Create the NAT Network (10.0.0.0/24)

  1. In VirtualBox Manager, open File → Tools → Network.
  2. Open the NAT Networks tab and click Create.
  3. Set Name to NatNetwork, IPv4 Prefix to 10.0.0.0/24, and keep Enable DHCP ticked.
  4. Click Apply.

VirtualBox creates the network with its default prefix of 10.0.2.0/24, so the prefix must be edited:

After the change the list shows 10.0.0.0/24 with the DHCP server enabled:

Step 4. Import Kali Linux and attach it to the NAT Network

Download the Kali VirtualBox image from https://kali.org/get-kali, extract it with 7-Zip, and add it to VirtualBox. Then open the VM's Settings → Network → Adapter 1:

Setting Value
Attached to NAT Network
Name NatNetwork
Promiscuous Mode Allow All

Step 5. Enable the shared clipboard and drag-and-drop

In Settings → General → Features, set Shared Clipboard and Drag-and-Drop to Bidirectional. In VirtualBox 7.2 these options sit under the Features tab.

Step 6. Share the host Downloads folder

In Settings → Shared Folders, add the Windows Downloads folder with Auto-mount ticked and Read-only unticked (full access).

Inside Kali the share appears as sf_Downloads and is mounted under /media/:

ls /media/sf_Downloads

Step 7. Set the static IP address in Kali

Run these in a Kali terminal (also available as scripts/set-static-ip.sh):

sudo nmcli connection modify "Wired connection 1" \
  ipv4.method manual \
  ipv4.addresses 10.0.0.2/24 \
  ipv4.gateway 10.0.0.1 \
  ipv4.dns 8.8.8.8 \
  ipv4.dad-timeout 0

sudo nmcli connection down "Wired connection 1"
sudo nmcli connection up "Wired connection 1"

ipv4.dad-timeout 0 turns off the duplicate-address-detection delay, a known fix for connectivity problems on VirtualBox 7 with recent Kali releases. If the DNS server does not respond, try the gateway (10.0.0.1) as the DNS server instead.

Step 8. Verify the IP address and internet access

ip a
ping -c 3 google.com

Step 9. Take a snapshot

With Kali powered off, open the VM's Snapshots view and take a snapshot named Kali_Lab_Ready_10.0.0.2. It is the known-good starting point I can restore at any time.

Check Result

Snapshot Kali_Lab_Ready_10.0.0.2 present

Problems I ran into

Problem Cause Fix
Kali had 10.0.2.15 instead of 10.0.0.2 VM adapter was on plain NAT, so VirtualBox's default network was used Attached the adapter to NAT Network and set the static IP
Name dropdown showed "Not selected" and OK was greyed out The NAT Network had not been created yet Created it under File → Tools → Network → NAT Networks
NAT Network came up as 10.0.2.0/24 VirtualBox default prefix Edited the IPv4 Prefix to 10.0.0.0/24 and applied
Clipboard and drag-and-drop options hard to find In VirtualBox 7.2 they moved to General → Features Set both to Bidirectional there
Add Share dialog had no "Access" dropdown Newer versions use a Read-only checkbox Left Read-only unticked for full access
